question: How the original's edit box takes keyboard input: focus, characters, editing keys, the caret, where its text is drawn, and Enter.

addresses.name: GuiObject_editBoxType::GuiObject_editBoxType
addresses.no_signature: the object is the first stack argument, the editBoxType type arrives in EDX, and three strings come by value: 40 dwords in all, `ret 0xA0`. In order: this, graphics, gui, textureFile (by value), font (by value), position (two shorts), text (by value), name (by value), size (two shorts), layer, &cursor offset, orientation, borderSize x, borderSize y, parent width, parent height
addresses.comment: Builds an `editBoxType` widget; called only by the type's builder 0xB29F80 (rva 0x729F80), which the window's factory 0xAC72B0 calls. CGuiObject's constructor, then the abstract base's table 0x15FECD8, then the CTextLayout base at +0x48 made with the gui's clipboard (gui +0x7C) and the font found by name (graphics +0x88 fonts, else +0x94 bitmapfonts); then the final tables 0x15FED90/0x15FEE50. Keeps graphics +0x100, font name +0x10C, textureFile +0x128, borderSize +0x144/+0x148, position +0x14C/+0x150, size +0x154, orientation +0x16C, parent size +0x170/+0x174, the `cursor = { x y }` offset +0x178/+0x17C, layer +0x180; editing and read_only (+0x158/+0x159) cleared. **Sets the layout's maximum length (+0x48+0xA0, i.e. +0xE8) to 250 (0xFA)** over the layout's own 1,000,000; the layout's area is the size less twice the border. Inserts the declared `text` through the layout's slot 21. +0x104 is a display object made from the element's name (graphics 0xA6FFB0), placed with GuiObject_editBoxType::PlaceAt; +0x168 a clock from the platform factory (g_random_object slot 1), started; **+0x108 the caret: the spriteType named `cursor`** (core.gfx: gfx/interface/textcursor.tga), made through graphics 0xA6FE30 and hidden at once (slot 14).
addresses.evidence: Read on the listing 0xA8F160-0xA8F5AE and checked against the builder's pushes 0xB29FBF-0xB2A0D0 (each type field to its argument by offset: +0x78 textureFile, +0x94 font, +0xD8 position, +0xB0 text, +0xE0 size, +0xE8 orientation, +0x68 borderSize, +0x70 cursor). `mov dword ptr [esi+0xe8], 0xfa` at 0xA8F2E3 with esi the widget and the layout at +0x48. Wrong if the builder pushed in another order than read.

addresses.name: GuiObject_editBoxType::OnInput
addresses.signature: void __thiscall GuiObject_editBoxType::OnInput(GuiObject_editBoxType* this, void* event, void* mouse)
addresses.comment: **Slot 1, the edit box's input handler**, called by CGui::ProcessInput with each event and the mouse. Event kind 0 (mouse) over the box (CGuiObject +0x2C) with the left button held (mouse slot 12, its +0x94): **clicked (+0x40) = 1** and the event handled - which is all a click does; the caret is not moved. Event kind 1 (key) only while shown (+0x43) and editing (+0x158): a code-0 message-0 event is swallowed; otherwise it goes on only if it is **a character (WM_CHAR, 0x102), or a key down of Left or Right with neither Ctrl nor Shift held (KeyEvent_IsPlainLeft/Right), Home (KeyEvent_IsHomeDown), End (KeyEvent_IsEndDown), or Delete (0x2E) without Shift**. Then: where the box's font (+0x10C, found in the fonts then the bitmapfonts) answers slot 19 true - CEU3BitmapFont's `effect` byte (+8), which defaults to yes - the bytes '"' 0x22, 0xA7, 0xA4, 0xA3, '@', '{' and '}' are refused; any byte on the box's own refused list (+0x188, filled by EditBox_RefuseCharacter) is refused; Tab (9) is refused. **A refused key returns without marking the event handled**, so it falls through to the next receiver. Anything else: the layout's HandleKey (slot 20) with (code, message), `typed` (+0x184) = 1, EditBox_RefreshText, and the event handled. `ret 8`.
addresses.evidence: Read whole on the listing 0xA8FD50-0xA8FE97 (the refusal compares at 0xA8FE33-0xA8FE4D, the list walk 0xA8FE54-0xA8FE69, Tab 0xA8FE6B). The font flag: CEU3BitmapFont table 0x15E13D4 slot 19 = 0xB00DC0 `mov al,[ecx+8]`, and CEU3BitmapFont::LoadKey's token 0x58 (`effect`, saveTokens.json) reads a yes/no into +8 (0xAF9D8A -> 0xA7B410); CBitmapFont's constructor writes +8 = 1 (0xAF9889). Wrong if a refused key were marked handled elsewhere.

addresses.name: GuiObject_editBoxType::Update
addresses.comment: Slot 6, run every frame by CGui::ProcessInput for each shown object. Only while shown and editing: **the blink** - the clock (+0x168) read in seconds; under 0.5 the phase (+0x160) is 0; strictly between 0.5 and 1 it is 1; at exactly 0.5 or at 1 or more the clock is reset and restarted and the phase kept. On a change of phase 0->1 the caret is hidden, 1->0 shown; **and where a key was taken this frame (`typed`, +0x184) it is hidden as well**, to come back at the next 1->0. Then the caret is placed: the box's anchored position (orientation +0x16C over the parent size) + border (+0x144/+0x148) + the `cursor` offset (+0x178/+0x17C) + the layout's caret pixel (slot 11; or, with a mask, slot 55 over the masked line +0x1B4), through the caret sprite's slot 51; `typed` cleared. `ret 4`.
addresses.evidence: Read on the listing 0xA8FEA0-0xA90130: `fld qword [0x160A308]` is the double 0.5; the three compares at 0xA8FED5, 0xA8FF01, 0xA8FF16; hide = sprite slot 14 (+0x38) at 0xA8FF5A, show = slot 13 (+0x34) at 0xA8FF73 (the same pair Show/Hide use on it). Clock slots per FINDINGS-tooltips.md section 3 (slot 5 seconds; slot 2 reset 0xB4FE40; slot 1 start).

addresses.name: EditBox_RefreshText
addresses.comment: **Hands the display object the one line the caret is on.** Where the display object (+0x104) exists: the layout's lines (slot 52, entries 0x20 bytes), the caret's row (slot 10, the high word of +0x38), held below the line count; that line's text - or, with a mask string at +0x198, the mask repeated once per character with newlines kept (also built into +0x1B4) - to the display's slot 61 with the font name, the textureFile, the size (w, h), the border (x, y) and 0, 0. So **the box shows one wrapped line, the caret's, and never more**. What the save dialog and the row click call after writing `game_name` (FINDINGS-ingamemenu.md C.3, C.4). 24 callers. `ret 4`.
addresses.evidence: Read on the listing 0xA90140-0xA903DD; the row is `movzx esi, word [esp+0x16]` of the dword slot 10 writes, clamped at 0xA9019F. Callers by findRefs --callers.

addresses.name: GuiObject_editBoxType::GainFocus
addresses.comment: Slot 20, which CGui::ProcessInput calls on the object becoming the keyboard focus: **unless read-only (+0x159), `editing` (+0x158) = 1 and the caret shown**. The caret is not moved. A read-only box takes the focus and does nothing with it.
addresses.evidence: Bytes 0xA90510-0xA9052D. The caller is 0xA7D5D8 (`call [edx+0x50]` on the clicked object).

addresses.name: GuiObject_editBoxType::LoseFocus
addresses.comment: Slot 21, called on the old focus before the new one gains it: `editing` (+0x158) = 0 and the caret hidden. Text and caret position are kept.

addresses.name: GuiObject_editBoxType::CanTakeFocus
addresses.comment: Slot 22: true where not read-only (+0x159) and shown (+0x43). The base answers false (ReturnFalse). No caller read; the name is inferred from what it tests.

addresses.name: EditBox_RefuseCharacter
addresses.comment: Appends a byte to the box's refused list (+0x188 head, +0x18C tail, +0x190 count; nodes 0x10 bytes, the byte at +0, next at +8), which OnInput tests every key against. **Two callers, both the console's set-up (0x60C055, 0x60C05F): 0xA7 and '`'**, the keys that toggle the console. Nothing else calls it, so `game_name` has an empty list. `ret 4`.
addresses.evidence: Bytes 0xA90570-0xA905C7; findRefs --callers finds exactly the two pushes `-0x59` and `0x60`. The positive control for the list is OnInput's walk at 0xA8FE54.

addresses.name: CTextLayout::SetText

addresses.name: CTextLayout::HandleKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CTextLayout::HandleKey(CTextLayout* this, int code, int message)
addresses.comment: **Slot 20, what a key does to the text.** Home key down: column 0. End key down: column = GetLineLength. A character (message 0x102): Backspace (8) -> slot 39 Backspace where the selection +0x50 is empty, else slot 40; Enter (13) -> only where there is no selection: a '\n' inserted where +0x98 is set (0 by default), then **every listener's slot 3**; any other byte, '$' and '#' included -> InsertText of that one byte. A key down (not 0x102): Delete without Shift -> slot 40 DeleteForward. Then for any event: Down 0x28 / Up 0x26 key down -> slots 31/30; with neither Ctrl nor Shift held, **code 0x27 -> slot 29 (CaretRight) and code 0x25 -> slot 27 (CaretLeft), whatever the message**; Ctrl+0x25 / Ctrl+0x27 -> slots 37/38 (by word); Shift+Left/Right key down -> slots 26/28 (extend the selection); Insert (0x2D) with Ctrl -> slot 50 (copy), with Shift -> slot 48 (paste). Through the edit box only characters, plain Left/Right, Home, End and Delete arrive (GuiObject_editBoxType::OnInput), so copy, paste, selection, words and Up/Down are unreachable there. `ret 8`.
addresses.evidence: Read whole on the listing 0xACC2E0-0xACC5F4: Home 0xACC303-0xACC32B, End 0xACC32E-0xACC35B, Backspace 0xACC36B, Enter 0xACC3D5 (the empty-selection test via 0x40C3C0, the newline string 0x15B57D0, listener walk 0xACC425-0xACC43E calling [vt+0xC]), the generic insert 0xACC442 through KeyEvent_ToText. The code 0x27/0x25 tests at 0xACC4FD/0xACC523 have no message test. Wrong if 0xAB8B10 made text out of a key down (it makes an empty string).

addresses.name: CTextLayout::InsertText
addresses.comment: Slot 21. A one-byte string whose byte is on the layout's refused list (+0x88; CTextLayout_RefuseDoubleQuote) does nothing. Otherwise by where the caret stands: at the end of the text CTextLayout_InsertAtEnd, at (0, 0) CTextLayout_InsertAtStart (column = the string's length), else CTextLayout_InsertAtCaret - **each of the three inserts nothing once the text already holds `max length` (+0xA0) bytes or more**, and inserts the whole string otherwise. The caret goes after what was inserted; the line count is rebuilt; where +0x9A is clear and an area height is set, Backspace runs until the lines fit the height and max lines (+0x9C) - +0x9A is set by default, so not in an edit box; then every listener's slot 2. `ret 4`.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled 0xACC600-0xACC7E6; the length tests `cmp edx,[ebx+0xa0]` 0xACE828, `cmp ecx,[edi+0xa0]` 0xACEA02, `cmp eax,[esi+0xa0]` 0xACEB6E are the only readers of +0xA0 in the class's code (disp scan of 0xACB000-0xACF300, which also finds the constructor's write as its positive control).

addresses.name: CTextLayout_SetCaretFromIndex
addresses.comment: Puts the caret at a character index of the text: the laid-out text up to it, the row = its count of '\n', the column = what follows the last one. `ret 4`. Read from a noisy decompilation; the name is the reading.

addresses.name: CTextLayout::GetLines
addresses.comment: Slot 52: the vector of laid-out lines at +0xA4 (entries 0x20 bytes: a Hoi3CString and, at +0x1C, a byte set where the line's last character is a break the wrap put in), rebuilt through slot 51 from the text when +0xB4 or +0xB5 is set.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled 0xACCA90-0xACCB0D; IndexOf subtracts the +0x1C byte per line.

addresses.name: CTextLayout::BuildLines
addresses.no_signature: the text comes by value (0x1C bytes) with a pointer to the vector after it: `ret 0x20`
addresses.comment: Slot 51, **the line breaker**: splits at '\n'; and unless +0x9B is set, **wraps a line whose width (font slot 10) plus the width of one 'O' (font slot 18) exceeds the area width (+0x48, the box less twice its border)** - at the last space that fits, else at the most characters that fit (0xACC960). addresses.comment: Code 0x25 (Left) with **neither Ctrl nor Shift held** (GetKeyState). `ret 4`.

addresses.name: KeyEvent_IsPlainRight
addresses.comment: Code 0x27 (Right) with neither Ctrl nor Shift held. `ret 4`.

addresses.name: KeyEvent_IsEndDown
addresses.no_signature: the input event in EAX, a bare `ret`, the answer in AL
addresses.comment: Code 0x23 (End) and not a character.

addresses.name: KeyEvent_IsShiftRight
addresses.no_signature: the input event in EAX, a bare `ret`, the answer in AL
addresses.comment: Code 0x27, not a character, Shift held.

addresses.name: KeyEvent_IsShiftLeft
addresses.no_signature: the input event in EAX, a bare `ret`, the answer in AL
addresses.comment: Code 0x25, not a character, Shift held.

addresses.name: KeyEvent_IsNavigationKey
addresses.no_signature: the event record {code, message} in ESI, the answer in AL, a bare `ret`
addresses.comment: **Which keys the window procedure (0xA91610) queues as key downs**, and which characters it drops. A key down is claimed (queued) where it is: Down, Up, plain Left/Right, Ctrl+Insert, Delete without Shift, Home, Ctrl+Left, Shift+Left, Shift+Right, Shift, Ctrl, Shift+Insert, Pause, Ctrl+Right, End, Escape, F1-F24 (0x70-0x87), Page Down, Page Up, or Tab. A character is claimed only where it is Tab (9) - and for a character, being claimed means **not** queued. Key downs not claimed are queued only while Ctrl is held. Settles FINDINGS-selection.md's frontier item 0x6800D0.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled 0xA800D0-0xA801F7 and the window procedure's two call sites read (WM_KEYDOWN queues on true or Ctrl; WM_CHAR queues on false, and only when Ctrl is up).

addresses.name: CGui::ProcessInput
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CGui::ProcessInput(CGui* this, void* mouse, void* keyboard, void* events)
addresses.comment: **CEU3Gui slot 1: the gui's pass over a frame's input events**, called by the screen before its own handler (CInGameIdler's at 0x651C2C, with its mouse +0x64, keyboard +0x1C and event list +0x1CB0). Keyboard kept at +0xA4; a keyboard focus (+0xA0) whose `released` (+0x2E) is set is dropped; the hovered object (+0x98) cleared. **A key event** goes first to the focus (+0xA0) where it is shown, then to each shown object of the vector +0x6C in turn (only those whose slot 2, has_focus, answers true where +0x12 is set) until one marks it handled. **A mouse event** goes to the objects under the pointer, topmost first, until one handles it. **A handled event is taken off the list** (or marked +0x24 where the list keeps its entries), so the screen's own handler never sees it. Then, unless +0x9C or +0x238: every shown object's slot 6 (Update) with the mouse; +0x2D = +0x2C, +0x2C = 0; and **the last object in the vector whose `clicked` (+0x40) was set - cleared as it is read - becomes the keyboard focus**: unless it is `released`; the old focus, unless it `keeps_focus` (+0x41) - in which case nothing changes - gets slot 21 (LoseFocus), the new one slot 20 (GainFocus), and +0xA0 = it. `ret 0xC`.
addresses.evidence: Read on the listing 0xA7D0F0-0xA7D60F (key branch 0xA7D28A-0xA7D334, mouse 0xA7D3E4-0xA7D460, focus 0xA7D564-0xA7D5E2). The caller's pushes at 0x651C1D-0x651C2C; CInGameIdler +0x1CBC, the list's keep byte, is written 0 at 0x648459 and nowhere else, so handled events are freed. Wrong if +0xA0 were written elsewhere with another meaning.

addresses.name: CGuiObject::OnPointerOver
addresses.comment: Slot 0 of CGuiObject's table: the pick's callback for an object under the pointer. `hovered` (+0x2C) = 1, or = (depth <= +0x3C) where +0x3C is not -1; and where +0x3C is above -2 and slot 23 answers true, **the gui's +0x98 = this** - the writer FINDINGS-tooltips.md said was not read. `ret 4`.
addresses.evidence: Bytes 0xA80000-0xA8003A. Held at slot 0 by CEU3DialogGui@0x18, CGraphicalTableLedger and CPieChartLedgerGraphical, all CGuiObject subclasses; the edit box's own table holds it at slot 0 too.

addresses.name: CGuiObject::Release
addresses.comment: The base's slot 12: `released` (+0x2E) = 1. Widgets override it to release their drawn objects first (the edit box's 0xA8F910, the text box's 0xA88080).
addresses.evidence: `mov byte ptr [ecx+0x2e],1; ret`. In the edit box base table 0x15FECD8 at slot 12 and in no RTTI table.

structs.name: GuiObject_editBoxType
structs.comment: A live `editBoxType` widget (vftable 0x11FED90; abstract base table 0x11FECD8; its CTextLayout base at +0x48 with table 0x11FEE50). 0x1D0 bytes. CGuiObject's fields are at their own offsets; not declared as inheriting because neither class is in the RTTI export. **The name is ours**, from the .gui keyword. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-editbox.md.
structs.evidence: The builder 0xB29F80 allocates 0x1D0 (`push 0x1d0` at 0xB29FA0), matching FINDINGS-guistatic.md's factory table and the live stride 0x1D8.

structs.name: CTextLayout
structs.comment: A word-wrapped, multi-line text with a caret, a selection, refused characters, a maximum length and a clipboard pointer; table 0x1202550, no RTTI, **the name ours**. The edit box holds one by value at +0x48, the tooltip text another. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-editbox.md.
structs.evidence: Its constructor writes up to the word at +0xB4, and in the edit box the next field after the base at +0x48 is +0x100 (graphics, written by the edit box's constructor at 0xA8F1E2): 0x100 - 0x48 = 0xB8. Wrong if the edit box padded after its base.

struct_fields.name: text
struct_fields.comment: The text, its caret and its lines: the second base, by value (table 0x11FEE50). Everything typed goes through its HandleKey (slot 20).
struct_fields.evidence: Constructed at 0xA8F1CE with `lea edi,[esi+0x48]`; table written 0xA8F1DC.

struct_fields.name: graphics
struct_fields.comment: The graphics the box's display, caret and font come from.
struct_fields.evidence: Written from the constructor's second argument at 0xA8F1E2; OnInput hands it to the font lookup 0xA6FBA0.

struct_fields.name: display
struct_fields.comment: The object that draws the box's background (textureFile, borderSize) and its one shown line - made from the element's name through graphics 0xA6FFB0; its slot 61 takes the text, its slot 51 the position, 13 and 14 show and hide. Its own drawing was not read.
struct_fields.evidence: Written at 0xA8F426; read by EditBox_RefreshText and Show/Hide.

struct_fields.name: caret
struct_fields.comment: The caret: a sprite of the spriteType `cursor` (interface/core.gfx, gfx/interface/textcursor.tga), slot 51 places it, 13 shows, 14 hides.
struct_fields.evidence: 0xA8F4C3-0xA8F504: the string 'cursor' handed to graphics 0xA6FE30, the result stored here and hidden (slot 14) at once.

struct_fields.name: font_name
struct_fields.comment: The `font` key; OnInput looks it up (fonts, then bitmapfonts) for its `effect` byte.
struct_fields.evidence: Assigned at 0xA8F31D from the font string argument; `lea esi,[ebx+0x10c]` before 0xA6FBA0 in OnInput.

struct_fields.name: texture_file
struct_fields.comment: The `textureFile` key, handed to the display with the text.

struct_fields.name: border_x
struct_fields.comment: `borderSize` x: added to the caret's x and handed to the display.
struct_fields.evidence: 0xA8F35B from the constructor's argument the builder takes from type +0x68.

struct_fields.name: border_y
struct_fields.comment: `borderSize` y.

struct_fields.name: declared_position
struct_fields.comment: The `position` as declared (two shorts); slot 46 (a body folded across three tables) answers it.

struct_fields.name: position
struct_fields.comment: The position the box stands at (two shorts), set by GuiObject_editBoxType::PlaceAt; the caret is placed from it.

struct_fields.name: size
struct_fields.comment: The `size` (two shorts, width then height).

struct_fields.name: editing
struct_fields.comment: **Whether the box is taking keys and showing its caret**: set by GainFocus (slot 20) unless read-only, and by slot 44; cleared by LoseFocus (slot 21). OnInput takes keys only while it and is_open are set.

struct_fields.name: read_only
struct_fields.comment: Set: GainFocus does not start editing, so nothing can be typed. CUnitView sets it on a row's `unitname` (0x769E30).
struct_fields.evidence: Tested in GainFocus and CanTakeFocus; written 1 at 0x769E30.

struct_fields.name: blink_phase
struct_fields.comment: 0 for the first half second of the caret clock, 1 for the second.

struct_fields.name: blink_phase_last
struct_fields.comment: The phase of the frame before; a change shows or hides the caret.

struct_fields.name: blink_clock
struct_fields.comment: A clock in seconds from the platform factory, restarted each time it reaches 1 (or exactly 0.5).

struct_fields.name: orientation
struct_fields.comment: The `orientation` as a number (0-6), anchoring the box and its caret to the parent.
struct_fields.evidence: 0xA8F23F from type +0xE8; the switch in GuiObject_editBoxType::PlaceAt and Update.

struct_fields.name: parent_width
struct_fields.comment: The parent's width, for the orientations that anchor right or centre.

struct_fields.name: parent_height
struct_fields.comment: The parent's height.

struct_fields.name: cursor_offset_x
struct_fields.comment: **The `cursor = { x y }` key's x**: added to the caret's position. No file of the base game sets it.
struct_fields.evidence: 0xA8F25F from the pointer the builder passes to type +0x70; LoadKey token 0x1B7 (`cursor`) writes type +0x70/+0x74.

struct_fields.name: cursor_offset_y
struct_fields.comment: The `cursor` key's y.

struct_fields.name: layer
struct_fields.comment: Handed to the display and the caret by SetLayer (slot 25). Inferred a draw layer.

struct_fields.name: typed
struct_fields.comment: Set by OnInput when a key reaches the text; Update hides the caret for it and clears it.

struct_fields.name: refused_chars
struct_fields.comment: Head of the box's own list of refused bytes (nodes 0x10: the byte at +0, next at +8; tail +0x18C, count +0x190). Only the console fills it, with 0xA7 and '`'.

struct_fields.name: mask
struct_fields.comment: A string shown in place of each character where not empty (a password mask). Empty from the constructor; no setter found.

struct_fields.name: masked_line
struct_fields.comment: The masked line EditBox_RefreshText builds; where not empty the caret is measured over it.

struct_fields.name: listeners
struct_fields.comment: Head of the list of listeners (nodes {listener, prev, next at +8}); slot 1 adds, slot 2 removes. Their slot 2 is told of a change (InsertText, Backspace), their slot 3 of Enter.

struct_fields.name: text
struct_fields.comment: The raw text, without the wrap's breaks; slot 19 answers it (the save button reads it so).
struct_fields.evidence: SetText, the insert helpers and EraseAt all write here.

struct_fields.name: desired_column
struct_fields.comment: The column to keep across Up/Down; -1 after CaretToLineEnd.

struct_fields.name: caret_column
struct_fields.comment: The caret's column in its laid-out line. With +0x3A it is one dword, column low.
struct_fields.evidence: HandleKey's Home writes 0 here; SetCaret writes the dword.

struct_fields.name: caret_row
struct_fields.comment: The caret's laid-out line.
struct_fields.evidence: GetCaretPixel multiplies it by the line height; EditBox_RefreshText reads the high word.

struct_fields.name: line_count
struct_fields.comment: The number of laid-out lines.
struct_fields.evidence: GetLineCount; InsertText and Backspace write it.

struct_fields.name: line_length
struct_fields.comment: The caret's line's length as last stored (insert, Backspace, Delete; not caret moves). End puts the caret here.

struct_fields.name: area_width
struct_fields.comment: The width lines wrap to; the edit box's size less twice its border. 256 by default.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor 0x400100 at +0x48; edit box constructor 0xA8F373; BuildLines compares against it.

struct_fields.name: area_height
struct_fields.comment: The height; InsertText trims to it only where +0x9A is clear.

struct_fields.name: insert_mode
struct_fields.comment: 1 by default: the insert helpers insert; 0 would overwrite. Inferred.
struct_fields.evidence: The insert helpers branch on it; constructor writes 1.

struct_fields.name: selection
struct_fields.comment: The selected text; empty when nothing is selected, which is what Backspace and Enter ask.

struct_fields.name: selecting
struct_fields.comment: A selection is open (slot 45 answers it).
struct_fields.evidence: SelectLeft/Right set it; slot 45 is `mov al,[ecx+0x6c]`.

struct_fields.name: clipboard
struct_fields.comment: The clipboard Copy writes and Paste reads: the gui's own string (gui +0x7C), not Windows'.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor's second argument; the edit box passes gui+0x7C (0xA8F1C6).

struct_fields.name: font
struct_fields.comment: The font measuring and wrapping use (slots 10, 11, 18).

struct_fields.name: refused_chars
struct_fields.comment: Head of the layout's own refused list (nodes {byte, ?, next at +8}); InsertText refuses a one-byte string on it. CTextLayout_RefuseDoubleQuote adds '"'.

struct_fields.name: newline_on_enter
struct_fields.comment: Set: Enter inserts '\n'. 0 by default; slot 54 sets it.

struct_fields.name: no_wrap
struct_fields.comment: Set: lines break only at '\n'. 0 by default. Inferred.

struct_fields.name: max_lines
struct_fields.comment: -1 for no limit; CUnitView sets 1 on `unitname`.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor 0xACBC6A; 0x769DD5 writes 1 through the edit box (+0xE4).

struct_fields.name: max_length
struct_fields.comment: **The most bytes an insert may start from**: an insert is refused once the text holds this many or more, and a longer string inserted below it is kept whole. 1,000,000 by default; **250 in every edit box**.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor 0xACBC74; the edit box's 0xA8F2E3; the three compares in the insert helpers.

struct_fields.name: lines
struct_fields.comment: Begin of the vector of laid-out lines (entries 0x20: a Hoi3CString and a byte at +0x1C set where the wrap put the line's break).

struct_fields.name: lines_dirty
struct_fields.comment: Set by every edit; GetLines rebuilds and clears it.

struct_fields.name: hovered
struct_fields.comment: Under the pointer this frame: set by OnPointerOver (slot 0), moved to +0x2D and cleared by CGui::ProcessInput after each frame's updates. The edit box's click test asks it.

struct_fields.name: hovered_last_frame
struct_fields.comment: +0x2C as it was at the end of the last frame.

struct_fields.name: released
struct_fields.comment: Set by slot 12 (Release). The gui drops a keyboard focus with it set, and a clicked object with it set does not take the focus.

struct_fields.name: clicked
struct_fields.comment: **Set to ask for the keyboard focus**: the edit box sets it on a press over it (with a word store, so +0x41 is cleared too), and code sets it to give a box the focus (OpenSaveDialog 0x66CB73 on `game_name`, the console's toggle 0x65380E on its box; eleven more word stores of 1 here, not read). CGui::ProcessInput reads and clears it after the frame's updates and hands the focus to the last object in its vector that had it.
struct_fields.evidence: A byte-pattern scan for stores of 1 at +0x40 (word and byte forms) over the gui code 0xA70000-0xB70000 finds the edit box's two (0xA8FD78, 0xA8F9D2) and, as word stores, nothing else; over the whole image thirteen more word stores, two read. Read and cleared at 0xA7D58E/0xA7D591.

struct_fields.name: keeps_focus
struct_fields.comment: Set on the keyboard focus: no click moves the focus away from it. 0 from the constructor; no writer of 1 found.

struct_fields.name: hovered_object
struct_fields.comment: The object under the pointer that answers for its tooltip: written by CGuiObject::OnPointerOver, cleared by each ProcessInput and by a dying object's destructor. FINDINGS-tooltips.md read it without its writer.

struct_fields.name: keyboard_focus
struct_fields.comment: **The object with the keyboard**: offered every key event first. Set by ProcessInput's focus step; dropped where it is `released`.
struct_fields.evidence: 0xA7D5E2, 0xA7D13E; the key branch reads it first.

struct_fields.name: keyboard
struct_fields.comment: The keyboard of the frame being processed (the screen's, CInGameIdler +0x1C). FINDINGS-scrollbar.md's 'gui's input object'.

1.name: CGui::ProcessInput
1.signature: void __thiscall CGui::ProcessInput(CGui* this, void* mouse, void* keyboard, void* events)

slots_noted: The edit box (0x11FED90), its base (0x11FECD8) and CTextLayout (0x1202550) have no RTTI, so their slots are recorded by naming the bodies and saying the slot in each comment, as FINDINGS-guistatic.md does for CFixedWindow. Folded bodies left unnamed: edit box slot 15 (0xA8F8F0, in three tables), slot 46 (0xB500B0, three), CTextLayout slot 10 (0xA48130, CDiplomacyStatus::GetValue) and slot 19 (0xACC920, CContinent::GetTag).
